## Learning objectives

We will use MyBinder for this workshop. You should be able to open the prepared workshop environment, load a verified copy of the teaching data, and prepare the dataset versions used in the hands-on activities. You will use the same project, dataset, and environment throughout the workshop.

## Our teaching dataset

We use `HealthWellbeing` from the
[correlations chapter](https://doing-meta.guide/pooling-es#pooling-cor)
[@harrer2021, sec. 4.2.4].
It contains study-level summaries of the association between health and
well-being. It is also distributed with the `dmetar` package.

The original review is @ngamaba2017. The dataset documentation describes
the variables [@healthwellbeing].

## Open the prepared environment {#choose-your-computing-environment}

MyBinder runs the workshop's published image in your browser, with RStudio, R 4.4.1, Git, Quarto, and the R packages recorded in the project lockfile already installed. There is nothing to install during the workshop.

1. [Open RStudio on MyBinder](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/HEAD?urlpath=rstudio)
   or use the link supplied by your instructor. Start it shortly before the
   workshop and keep the browser tab open; MyBinder stops idle sessions.
2. MyBinder sessions are temporary. Export any important work before closing your session.

## Check the project {#preparation-project}

You do not need to clone anything. MyBinder opens RStudio with the
workshop project already in your home folder, `/home/rstudio`. This
folder is the project root: the **Files** pane shows `pages`,
`pipelines`, `data`, and `open-and-reproducible-science-in-r.Rproj`.
The lessons' paths, such as `pipelines/prepare_health_wellbeing.R`, are
relative to this folder, so run every command from here.

The project's `.Rprofile` activates renv. Check your R version and whether the
library matches the lockfile. If the library in your MyBinder session differs
from the lockfile, check with the instructor before proceeding.

```{r health-preparation-environment, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
withr::with_dir(
  here::here(),
  source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
)
use_workshop_book_outputs()

R.version.string
renv::status()
```

## Verify the raw data {#preparation-data}

Run the following in the **R Console** from the project root. This will download and inspect the meta-analysis dataset.

```{r health-preparation-download, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
raw_file <- here::here("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
source_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MathiasHarrer/dmetar/",
  "38c9b9bb5f85ea49de33e5d2536f6544d5268517/data/HealthWellbeing.rda"
)

dir.create(dirname(raw_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(raw_file)) {
  download.file(source_url, destfile = raw_file, mode = "wb")
}

data_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
loaded_names <- load(raw_file, envir = data_env)
stopifnot(identical(loaded_names, "HealthWellbeing"))
health <- data_env[["HealthWellbeing"]]

withr::with_dir(
  here::here(),
  source("pipelines/prepare_health_wellbeing.R")
)

head(health, 5)
```

We should get **29 rows and 5 columns**, with no assertion failures.

## Preparation checkpoint {#preparation-checkpoint}

You are ready when:

- RStudio is open in MyBinder, or in your own prepared setup, at the project
  root.
- You know your R version and `renv::status()` reports no problems.
- The meta-analysis dataset is downloaded.

Continue to the
[introduction, reproducibility principles, Git and GitHub](01_open_science.qmd).
